thread.title: Apple Gets Burned on the Street, Shares Fall Into a Correction | Investopedia

author: investopedia.com
title: Apple Gets Burned on the Street, Shares Fall Into a Correction | Investopedia
text:
Apple Inc. ( AAPL ), the first U.S. corporation to reach a $1 trillion market capitalization earlier this year, has fallen into correction territory as of Wednesday. Trading down 2.3% at $187.92, shares of the Cupertino, Calif.-based tech titan are off 20% from highs reached in October, as investors become more fearful of a slowdown in the company's core iPhone business.
Bears Fear Higher ASPs Will Not Offset Lower Unit Sales While Apple bulls have cheered the firm's swift transition towards its higher-margin, recurring revenue software and services businesses, such as Apple Music and the App Store, the company still generates nearly 60% of its top line from its iPhone segment. With a handful of key suppliers offering warning signs of lower order requests from a major supplier , many on the Street are becoming more cautious on Apple stock, doubting that higher average selling prices (ASP) can offset a slowdown in iPhone demand.
Guggenheim Partner analysts downgraded shares of the global tech behemoth from buy to neutral on Wednesday, predicting a 5% decline in iPhone units sold in 2019, as outlined by CNBC . Guggenheim's Robert Cihra removed his previous 12 month price forecast of $245, writing that, "unlike last year [we] do not see ASP (average selling price) increases providing enough offset, with our forecast that blended iPhone ASPs increase only +3%Y/Y, leaving iPhone revenues -2%Y/Y."
Cihra cited softer iPhone unit demand, with downside in China, India and other emerging markets, "where Apple may need to start considering lower price points." Apple faces off against a handful of low-cost smartphone makers in China, such as Huawei Technologies.
Echoing the downbeat sentiment, UBS cut its Apple price target from $240 to $225 and lowered its iPhone unit sales estimates for the current quarter to 73.5 million from 75 million. UBS analyst Tim Arcuri pointed to news from Apple Face ID recognition supplier Lumentum ( LITE ) earlier this week, indicating that "cuts are significantly less than LITE new would imply." Ultimately, however, UBS views FX headwinds and heightened competitive pressures in China, which threaten the new iPhone XR in particular, as weighing on Apple stock.
On Tuesday, analysts at Goldman lowered their Apple price target to $209 from $222, warning on "deteriorating" end demand for new iPhone models.
